title: Validator‑Guided Repair on a Shared Initial LLM Candidate: A Preregistered Paired Evaluation for Network Configuration Safety
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01) to measure the downstream effect of a deterministic validator plus at most one automated repair on the same sampled LLM candidate per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics). Using the declared generator gpt‑5‑mini (hosted adapter) and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 on N=200 paired intents (completed_episode_count = 400; model_calls_used = 200), every shared sampled candidate passed validation and no repairs were attempted or applied (repair_attempt_count = 0; repair_applied_count = 0). Observed outcomes: baseline_success = 200/200, guarded_success = 200/200; paired contingency n11=200, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0]. We present artifact‑grounded methodology, representative validator diagnostics, explicit reproducibility pointers to archived artifacts and hashes, and a focused discussion clarifying that the executed estimand isolates downstream validator/repair effects under shared_initial_candidate semantics and therefore cannot measure repair efficacy under independent per‑condition sampling.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into device configurations in Network Operations (NetOps). LLM outputs can include syntactic errors, incorrect command ordering, or hallucinated fields that risk redundancy, availability, or policy violations if executed. Generate–validate–repair (GVR) architectures—where a generator produces a candidate, a deterministic validator detects violations, and an automated repair is optionally applied—are often proposed to mitigate these risks. Prior work documents hallucination and suggests evidence‑grounding or verifier‑guided feedback reduces incorrect artifacts in adjacent domains (e.g., IaC, program repair) but leaves open whether such pipelines reduce executable misconfigurations at device‑execution granularity in NetOps [1]–[5].

This paper reports a fully preregistered paired confirmatory experiment that implemented the shared_initial_candidate estimand: for each intent, exactly one sampled initial generation was produced and deterministically reused for both baseline (no validator/repair) and guarded (validator + ≤1 repair) arms. Under these semantics any paired difference can only arise from downstream validation/repair applied to that identical candidate; sampling variability across conditions is excluded by design. Our contributions are: (1) an artifact‑grounded report of the executed paired experiment (N=200 pairs) with validator traces and execution accounting; (2) exact inferential results for the executed estimand showing a degenerate null effect and diagnostics explaining why repairs never executed; and (3) concrete, artifact‑grounded follow‑on estimand designs and preregistered recommendations to evaluate repair efficacy under independent sampling, increased task difficulty, or adversarial uplift.
sections.related_work:
Hallucination and unreliable references in LLM outputs are a well documented reliability problem that motivates grounding, verification, and retrieval strategies [1]. Retrieval‑ and evidence‑grounded pipelines reduce hallucination for operations‑style QA, though those works typically measure textual correctness rather than device‑level executability in packet‑level simulators [2]. Generate→verify→repair architectures have demonstrated improvements for infrastructure‑as‑code and program generation by closing the loop with deterministic checks and feedback to the generator (e.g., TerraFormer and program‑repair demonstrations) [3,4]. These demonstrations motivate analogous NetOps pipelines but do not present standardized execution‑level device emulation results in the supplied records. Recent NetOps LLM evaluations focus on intent translation and capability measurement; an execution‑level safety benchmark in packet‑level simulation is not present among the verified corpus and motivated our preregistered confirmatory test [5].

We position our work deliberately: rather than benchmarking generator capability broadly, we isolate the marginal effect of deterministic validation and a single automated repair on an identical sampled candidate per intent. This narrow estimand complements prior work by making explicit the causal boundary between sampling variability and downstream validator/repair intervention.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The experiment was preregistered as PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01 prior to any model calls. The primary estimand is the paired difference in the proportion of validator‑valid executable configurations between guarded and baseline conditions under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The design fixed task_count = 200 paired intents and allowed at most one automated repair per guarded episode; generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate so each pair reused the same sampled initial generation. The primary confirmatory test was an exact two‑sided McNemar test with alpha = 0.05 and paired bootstrap CI (seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples).

Task bank and contamination controls. A deterministic task generator produced a fixed manifest of 200 synthetic 'intent_configuration_repair_v1' tasks; each manifest entry includes initial_state, required_sequence, difficulty annotation, and a generation_seed for deterministic replay. Preexecution contamination checks (SHA‑256 exact‑match and high‑similarity n‑gram thresholds) were run as preregistered; no exact‑match exclusions were flagged and the confirmatory sample remained intact. The task manifest and per‑task generation seeds are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl (hash: 08e3c8e4604ad8ffa9cbb5fab6be7624adb44e147457b47e49f6c48b73bd9ce9).

Model configuration and sampling semantics. The declared generator was gpt‑5‑mini via a hosted adapter (provider label openai_responses). The archived execution/model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt‑5‑mini" and temperature = null (unset). We explicitly report that temperature = null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; nondeterministic sampling remains possible. The provider audit recorded hosted_model_call_event_count = 200 and a single stage labeled shared_initial_generation = 200, consistent with the preregistered one‑sample per pair sampling semantics. The provider audit and model configuration are archived (model_configuration.json hash: a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820).

Validator and repair pipeline. Scoring used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 with scoring_rule = "full_intent_constraint_validation" producing binary executable/invalid labels and structured validator traces (validation_before/after, normalized_configuration, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes). For guarded episodes a single automated repair attempt was permitted (preregistered maximum_repair_calls_per_task = 1). Under shared_initial_candidate semantics the baseline condition reused the same sampled candidate without repair; only the guarded arm could alter that same candidate via the permitted repair if validator detections occurred. All per‑episode validator traces and repair metadata are archived under execution/scoring/*.json (examples and hashes below).
sections.results:
Execution accounting. The execution manifest reports planned_episode_count = 400, completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, model_calls_used = 200 (one shared initial generation per pair), and completed_pair_count = 200. The analysis missingness summary reports complete_pairs = 200 and zero failed or unscorable episodes; deterministic reconciliation confirms all consistency checks passed (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json hash: d2d4e1900e567eb98db7aa545c14f93d5f83f995fe171e9461b1942e951a1dff).

Primary outcomes. Per‑condition summaries are baseline_successes = 200/200 and guarded_successes = 200/200 (success_rate = 1.0 for each condition). The paired contingency table observed n11 = 200, n10 = 0, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the paired difference (bootstrap_seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples) = [0.0, 0.0]. These analytic artifacts are archived under analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (hash: 7bc1bd2a42b5ac3f7adb61db47cf8dbe0472f678032abcd1e7c44f92ea2de71c) and analysis/condition_summary.csv (hash: 1cb072b4db7c8e29212ef28b97baccb66a507a7c8b8ceaad35b7e84f7976a951).

Repair activity and representative diagnostics. Across the confirmatory sample repair_attempt_count = 0 and repair_applied_count = 0 because no shared initial candidate triggered a validator violation. Representative per‑episode JSON artifacts (e.g., execution/scoring/task-000004-baseline.json hash: 46847f2135dfc9461549656cb6849e166a5dfc8b7b82c34ecc7eebc7b376001c) show identical shared_initial_candidate text and identical validation_after.normalized_configuration for both baseline and guarded. Example (task‑000004 shared initial candidate): "interface edge2 admin down\ninterface edge2 vlan 40\ninterface edge2 admin up\ninterface edge1 admin down" with parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, validator.valid = true. Table 3 (below) summarizes the repair accounting and provides exact artifact pointers and hashes.

Contamination, provider audit, and reconciliation. Preexecution contamination checks flagged no exact‑match leaks; analysis/contamination_summary.csv is empty (hash: 389227f0d1e81239c7498abd4944a04c59c92c5fa042b990e332796cd61c3222). Provider audit shows hosted_model_call_event_count = 200, cache_hit_count = 0, cache_miss_count = 200, and stage_counts indicating shared_initial_generation = 200. All deterministic consistency checks passed and are archived (execution manifest hash references included in the evidence bundle).
sections.discussion:
Causal scope and interpretation. Because the experiment executed shared_initial_candidate semantics, it isolates only the downstream effect of validation/repair on identical sampled candidates. The degenerate null result—no discordant pairs—stems from the fact that every sampled candidate satisfied the deterministic validator and thus no repair trigger occurred. Therefore the study provides valid evidence that, for the chosen task bank, model sampling seeds, and validator fidelity, guarded repair could not alter outcomes; it does not evaluate whether independent sampling or alternative prompting would yield more validator‑detectable faults.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: the paired design intentionally eliminates sampling variability across conditions; this strengthens causal attribution for downstream validator/repair effects on the same candidate but precludes inference about sampling or prompt interventions. Construct validity: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 enforces a preregistered mapping from intent constraints to checks (syntax, required sequence, dependency rules, protected interfaces), but it is an abstraction that does not execute vendor CLI or packet‑level runtime behavior; timing and protocol interactions are therefore outside the validator's coverage. External validity: results reflect one declared generator (gpt‑5‑mini via hosted adapter), one synthetic task bank, and one validator; generalization to other models, real operational corpora, or higher‑fidelity validators is unsupported by these artifacts. Conclusion validity: the observed absence of discordant outcomes prevents estimation of repair effect size under independent sampling; claims about repair efficacy under broader conditions require new preregistered estimands.

Operational implications and recommended follow‑on estimands. The artifact record allows concrete follow‑on preregistered experiments that alter the estimand to measure repair efficacy under conditions where repairs can act: (A) independent per‑condition sampling (remove shared_initial_candidate) so repairs may observe additional validator failures; (B) difficulty uplift by selecting high‑difficulty or adversarially perturbed tasks to increase validator failure rate; (C) explicit sampling sweeps by setting non‑null numeric temperature values in model_configuration.json and preregistering sampling budgets; (D) validator fidelity uplift via vendor CLI semantics or packet‑level emulation to capture runtime failure modes. Each proposed follow‑on is supported by the archived task manifest and execution pipeline artifacts and constitutes a distinct preregistered estimand.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory experiment that measured the downstream effect of deterministic validation and at most one automated repair on the identical sampled LLM candidate per intent (shared_initial_candidate semantics). With gpt‑5‑mini as the declared generator and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as the scorer, every shared initial candidate passed validation and no repairs were attempted or applied; guarded and baseline outcomes were identical for the executed estimand (paired difference = 0.0; McNemar p = 1.0; paired bootstrap CI = [0.0, 0.0]). This narrow, artifact‑grounded result shows there was no opportunity for repair to change outcomes under the sampled tasks and preregistered sampling semantics. It does not imply that GVR pipelines are unnecessary in general. Follow‑on preregistered experiments (independent sampling, adversarial/difficulty uplift, explicit temperature settings, and higher‑fidelity validators) are required to assess repair effectiveness under realistic sampling variability and adversarial conditions. The archived artifacts, validator traces, and reconciliation logs support independent verification and exact replay of the executed estimand. (Reminder: the executed estimand intentionally used shared_initial_candidate semantics; an independent per‑condition sampling estimand would be a different preregistered experiment.)

disclosure_statement: Disclosure (concise): The human Research Director selected the broad topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) prior to the autonomy lock. After the autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature review, experiment selection, preregistration (PREREG‑CAND‑001‑VER‑GVR‑2026‑09‑01), code generation, execution, deterministic validation, automated analysis, and manuscript drafting without manual human editing of technical content. Declared model used in execution: gpt‑5‑mini via hosted adapter 'openai_responses' (execution used model_calls_used = 200; execution/model_configuration.json records temperature = null/unset; null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0). Generation semantics executed: shared_initial_candidate — exactly one sampled initial generation per intent was produced and deterministically reused for both baseline and guarded conditions (no independent per‑condition first‑pass sampling). Validator: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 scored candidates using 'full_intent_constraint_validation' and a single automated repair iteration was permitted in guarded episodes; in this run the validator flagged no violations and no repairs were applied (repair_attempt_count = 0; repair_applied_count = 0). Execution accounting: completed_episode_count = 400 (200 paired intents) completed without preregistration deviations; execution manifest and analysis artifacts are archived (see execution/* and analysis/*). Master prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt — 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba. Pre‑lock infrastructure development and rehearsal occurred but pre‑lock artifacts were not used as empirical evidence in this final run. After the autonomy lock no human manually rewrote technical results, manuscript text, figures, or references.
limitations: Shared_initial_candidate semantics: the design produced exactly one sampled initial generation per intent and reused it across baseline and guarded conditions; this measures validator/repair effects only and cannot detect differences caused by independent per‑condition sampling or prompt engineering.

Temperature unset (temperature = null) in the archived model configuration: null/unset is not evidence of deterministic sampling and does not imply temperature = 0; sampling nondeterminism may still have occurred during the single sampled generation.
Single model and single hosted provider: results reflect gpt‑5‑mini under the archived adapter; generalization to other models or model families is unsupported by these artifacts.

Synthetic task bank and validator abstraction: tasks were synthetic 'intent_configuration_repair_v1' items and the deterministic validator is an abstraction; realistic vendor CLI idiosyncrasies, emergent runtime interactions, and hardware effects were not executed on live devices.

No observed validator failures: all initial candidates were validator‑valid, so the experiment could not assess the repair step's effectiveness; the null effect therefore reflects the task bank and sampling semantics rather than evidence that GVR is unnecessary in general.
